question: Which service is provided in a Comprehensive EmONC (CEmONC) facility that is NOT part of a basic facility?

options.A: Basic neonatal resuscitation training
options.B: Provision of iron and folic acid supplements
options.C: Blood transfusions and caesarean sections
options.D: Administration of routine tetanus vaccines

explanation: Major surgeries like caesarean sections and blood banking are what upgrade a facility from basic to comprehensive EmONC. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h5)

question: Why should nurses rotate injection sites for patients who need frequent medications?

options.A: It ensures the medication reaches the bloodstream much faster
options.B: It stops bacteria from multiplying on the surface of the skin
options.C: It gives previous tissue time to heal instead of forming hard scar tissue
options.D: It prevents the needle from becoming dull during the procedure

explanation: Sticking the exact same spot over and over causes fibrous scar knots, which hurt the patient and make drug absorption difficult. Rotating sites keeps tissue healthy! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason hospitals use standardized usability questionnaires for electronic health records?

options.A: To test the speed of the hospital internet server cables
options.B: To measure user satisfaction and ease of use in a structured way
options.C: To calculate the financial budget for buying new computers
options.D: To check if the computer hardware is physically clean

explanation: Exactly! These questionnaires give hospitals a clear, reliable score on whether their software is actually user-friendly for nurses. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which group of nutrients does the body need in large amounts?

options.A: Macronutrients
options.B: Micronutrients
options.C: Trace elements
options.D: Antioxidants

explanation: Macro means large! Macronutrients like carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need in heavy quantities every day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h3)

question: What is sampling bias?

options.A: The deliberate refusal of a patient to answer survey questions
options.B: A systematic flaw where the selection process favors certain outcomes
options.C: An error made by a laboratory technician reading a blood test
options.D: The natural difference between a sample result and the population

explanation: Correct! Sampling bias happens when our selection method accidentally leans too much toward one side, so the sample doesn't truly reflect reality. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h6)

question: A pregnant patient is struggling with morning sickness and finds it hard to eat three big meals. What is the best advice?

options.A: Force yourself to eat large plates of heavy food to keep your strength up
options.B: Eat small, frequent snacks throughout the day to keep something in the stomach
options.C: Drink strong coffee on an empty stomach to wake up your digestive tract
options.D: Stop drinking all fluids completely until the vomiting stops entirely

explanation: An empty stomach can actually make nausea worse! Nibbling on small, light snacks often helps keep the tummy settled. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h5)

question: How do modern smart-speaker voice assistants help someone with severe vision loss?

options.A: They completely restore damaged optic nerves over time
options.B: They allow hands-free control of timers, reminders, and information
options.C: They serve as physical walking canes inside the house
options.D: They automatically administer prescribed glaucoma eye drops

explanation: Voice assistants are wonderful tools! They let users set alarms, check the weather, and make calls just by speaking, bypassing the need to read a screen. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the main job of satellite cells in our skeletal muscles?

options.A: To repair and regenerate damaged muscle fibers
options.B: To remove lactic acid buildup after heavy exercise
options.C: To store calcium ions needed for sliding filaments
options.D: To produce the nerve signals that trigger contraction

explanation: Satellite cells are like little standby repair crew members. When muscle gets injured, they jump in to help fix and rebuild it! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h5)

question: During a home visit, what is a key sign of neglect that a community health nurse should look for?

options.A: Frequent attendance at youth club meetings
options.B: A high grade point average in primary school
options.C: Poor hygiene and delayed physical growth milestones
options.D: Excessive participation in neighborhood sports

explanation: Physical signs like poor hygiene and stunted growth point directly to a lack of proper care, food, and supervision at home. Excellent assessment skill to master! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h5)

question: What happens to a DRF if hospital staff constantly collect drugs on credit and fail to pay back?

options.A: The suppliers will double the credit period for future orders
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically start generating higher profits
options.C: The fund will quickly experience cash depletion and stockouts
options.D: The government will automatically inject fresh emergency funds

explanation: Unpaid credit creates holes in the system. If the cash doesn't come back in, the pharmacy won't have money to buy new medicines when patients need them. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: What happens during a pharmacokinetic drug interaction?

options.A: One drug changes how the body absorbs, metabolizes, or excretes another drug.
options.B: The manufacturing company changes the active chemical ingredients.
options.C: Two drugs fight each other directly on the surface of the skin.
options.D: The patient develops an allergic skin rash from eating certain foods.

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as what the body does to the drug. If one drug messes with how the body handles another (like blocking liver breakdown), that's an interaction! [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h3)

question: A rural clinic lacks basic drugs and staff because government funds are delayed. What is the biggest immediate risk to patients?

options.A: Being overcharged by government health insurance schemes
options.B: Receiving free specialized surgeries at the local facility
options.C: Avoiding needed care or experiencing worsened health conditions
options.D: Enjoying excess medication supplies stored in the pharmacy

explanation: When clinics are empty and unfunded, sick people stay home, delay getting help, and unfortunately risk getting much worse. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which quality of a study means that if you repeat it, you will get consistent results?

options.A: Reliability
options.B: Neutrality
options.C: Generalizability
options.D: Randomization

explanation: Spot on! Reliability means your tools and methods are dependable and give consistent answers every time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h5)

question: How can partnering with farmers and the agricultural sector help improve community health?

options.A: It provides direct medical treatment for infectious diseases inside farms
options.B: It helps combat malnutrition by improving local food production
options.C: It replaces the need for primary healthcare clinics entirely
options.D: It trains farmers to perform minor surgical procedures in villages

explanation: Well done! Agriculture directly affects food security, which is key to preventing malnutrition in our communities. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h3)

question: Why do we view disaster management as an endless cycle rather than a straight line?

options.A: Because recovery takes the exact same amount of time as mitigation
options.B: Because lessons learned during recovery directly inform future mitigation and preparedness
options.C: Because disasters always happen at the exact same time every year
options.D: Because emergency personnel never stop responding to disasters

explanation: Brilliant! Every time we recover from a disaster, we learn valuable lessons that help us get better prepared for the next one. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which type of insurance policy covers incidents that happened while the policy was active, even if someone sues years later?

options.A: Group indemnity policy
options.B: Occurrence-based policy
options.C: Temporary health policy
options.D: Claims-made policy

explanation: Occurrence policies give you lifetime protection for any event that happened during the policy period, no matter how long after the fact the lawsuit is filed. [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which human factor frequently causes industrial accidents in the workplace?

options.A: Strict adherence to international building codes
options.B: Regular maintenance of old electrical grids
options.C: Operator fatigue and bypassed safety checks
options.D: Excessive routine safety training for workers

explanation: Well done! When workers are exhausted or skip safety rules to save time, accidents are much more likely to happen. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h3)

question: A toddler arrives at the emergency unit suddenly drooling, making high-pitched breathing sounds (stridor), and very restless, but has no cough. What should you do first?

options.A: Keep the child calm and avoid invasive examinations
options.B: Immediately force the child to lie flat for an X-ray
options.C: Attempt to visualize the vocal cords with a tongue depressor
options.D: Administer oral fluids immediately to soothe the throat

explanation: This sounds like epiglottitis! If you upset or cry the child, their swollen airway can snap shut completely. Keep them calm in their mother's arms and don't force anything into their mouth. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h5)

question: When a nurse uses skinfold calipers, which specific layer of tissue are they measuring?

options.A: Visceral fat
options.B: Subcutaneous fat
options.C: Deep fascia
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Correct! Calipers pinch and measure the layer of fat that lives right underneath the skin (subcutaneous fat). [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h6)

question: During which stage of team development does open conflict and friction typically peak?

options.A: Norming
options.B: Forming
options.C: Performing
options.D: Storming

explanation: Storming is marked by power struggles and clashes as members express their individual ideas. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h3)

question: A patient tests positive for HIV at the clinic. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient's name to local community leaders immediately
options.B: Advise the patient to stop working and isolate at home forever
options.C: Provide compassionate post-test counseling and link the patient to treatment services
options.D: Wait until the patient asks questions before saying anything about treatment

explanation: A positive test can be scary. As a nurse, your warmth, privacy, and gentle guidance are vital to connect them straight to the care they need. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why would a doctor prescribe the medication sucralfate for a duodenal ulcer?

options.A: It permanently neutralizes all digestive enzymes
options.B: It relaxes the pyloric sphincter to speed up digestion
options.C: It stimulates the pancreas to release more insulin
options.D: It forms a protective coating over the ulcer site

explanation: Great job! Sucralfate acts like a liquid bandage, sticking directly to the ulcer base to shield it from harsh stomach acids and pepsin. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T7#GNS213_U3_T7_h5)

question: What does a 'null hypothesis' usually say about two groups being compared?

options.A: The first group always has a higher score
options.B: The second group received a better treatment
options.C: There is no real difference between them
options.D: There are not enough patients in the study

explanation: The null hypothesis assumes a boring baseline: that your new treatment didn't actually do anything special and the groups are essentially the same. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is the correct order of steps in a PDSA quality cycle?

options.A: Prepare, Design, Survey, Assess
options.B: Plan, Do, Study, Act
options.C: Predict, Document, Solve, Apply
options.D: Prioritize, Delegate, Supervise, Audit

explanation: Spot on! PDSA stands for Plan, Do, Study, Act. It’s your trusty roadmap for testing small changes on the ward step by step. [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do learning management systems particularly benefit nurses who work rotating shift duties?

options.A: By allowing them to complete mandatory training modules at their own convenience
options.B: By exempting them from all practical hospital exams and clinical hours
options.C: By providing free mobile phones for personal communication use
options.D: By automatically writing their patient care notes during night shifts

explanation: Because these platforms are available online around the clock, nurses can fit their continuing education around irregular shift schedules. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h5)

question: What should health education focus on most for younger primary school children?

options.A: Advanced reproductive physiology and anatomy
options.B: Occupational hazard management in industries
options.C: Basic hygiene like handwashing and dental care
options.D: Chronic disease pharmacology and medication doses

explanation: Correct! Little ones benefit the most from mastering everyday self-care routines that keep common germs away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h5)

question: Which process is safe to use directly on living human skin?

options.A: High-level disinfection
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Incineration
options.D: Antisepsis

explanation: Antiseptics are formulated to be gentle on living skin. Strong sterilizing chemicals would cause chemical burns, ouch! [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the main job of a patient referral form in community health?

options.A: To replace the patient's daily hospital bed ticket
options.B: To serve as a permanent financial receipt for clinic services
options.C: To connect a patient with higher levels of specialized care
options.D: To discharge a patient permanently from all medical follow-up

explanation: You've got this! Referral forms act like a bridge, safely moving a patient from our basic community clinics up to advanced centers when they need extra specialist attention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is the main focus of long-term care compared to acute care?

options.A: Performing emergency procedures and trauma resuscitation
options.B: Providing short-term surgical recovery and rapid discharge
options.C: Maintaining quality of life and managing chronic conditions
options.D: Curing acute infections and stabilizing vital signs

explanation: You've got this! While acute care focuses on sudden illnesses, long-term care is all about steady, ongoing support and helping people live well with long-standing health challenges. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: To check the outer muscles that move the eyeball around
options.B: To view the internal structures of the back of the eye
options.C: To test the patient for clear distance and reading vision
options.D: To measure the exact fluid pressure inside the eyeball

explanation: Ophthalmoscopy specifically directs light through the pupil to examine the internal fundus, which includes the retina and optic disc. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h1)

question: When a researcher collects 'primary data', what are they doing?

options.A: Records taken from old hospital admission logs from ten years ago
options.B: Data published in international textbooks without any author names
options.C: Information collected directly by the researcher for the current study
options.D: Information guessed by the nurse without asking the patient

explanation: That's correct! Primary data is freshly gathered firsthand by the investigator specifically for their current study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h2)

question: What is a protective factor for mental health?

options.A: Strong family and social support systems
options.B: A family history of severe psychiatric illness
options.C: Experiencing severe trauma during childhood
options.D: Growing up in an environment of chronic poverty

explanation: Protective factors like social support help shield individuals from stress and lower the likelihood of mental health problems. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h3)

question: How does counselling differ from simple guidance?

options.A: Counselling avoids discussing personal emotions
options.B: Counselling focuses strictly on career choices
options.C: Counselling only deals with physical symptoms
options.D: Counselling focuses on internal feelings and behaviors

explanation: While guidance gives direction, counselling digs a bit deeper into a person's emotions and psychological state. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h2)

question: What is the popular local name for the skin boils caused by tumbu fly larvae in West Africa?

options.A: Guinea worm blister
options.B: Ground itch
options.C: Mango fly boil or 'tsoro'
options.D: Jigger foot

explanation: Tumbu fly larvae burrow under the skin to form raised, boil-like sores that locals commonly call mango fly boils or 'tsoro'. Excellent local clinical context! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is it important to know a germ's 'portal of exit' when caring for an infectious patient?

options.A: It calculates the total number of pathogens living inside the host.
options.B: It helps predict how the pathogen might leave the body to spread to others.
options.C: It determines the specific blood type compatibility of the host.
options.D: It reveals the exact genetic mutation rate of the invading organism.

explanation: Spot-on! Understanding the portal of exit shows you how germs leave the body (like through coughs or body fluids) so you can put up barriers and stop them. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: A ward speeds up patient discharge paperwork. To ensure this doesn't cause patients to return with sudden complications, what should they track?

options.A: Structural measure
options.B: Balancing measure
options.C: Process measure
options.D: Cost-saving measure

explanation: You're crushing it! Balancing measures help us keep an eye out for unexpected side effects when we change how we do things in the ward. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main job of an antigen in the body?

options.A: To trigger an immune system response
options.B: To destroy healthy body cells directly
options.C: To produce red blood cells in bone marrow
options.D: To transport oxygen throughout the bloodstream

explanation: Think of antigens as 'foreign flags.' When the body spots them, it sounds the alarm to start an immune defense! [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the main reason for frequently cleaning high-touch surfaces in an isolation room?

options.A: To prevent germs from surviving on objects and spreading
options.B: To prevent medical equipment from rusting
options.C: To make the floor shiny and slip-resistant
options.D: To keep the room smelling fresh for visitors

explanation: Pathogens can live on dry surfaces for hours or days, making regular disinfection vital to stopping indirect spread. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: When managing an infectious disease, why should a community nurse look beyond just the individual patient?

options.A: Because individual treatments are rarely effective against infections
options.B: To comply with hospital administrative discharge policies
options.C: To prevent the illness from spreading to other members of the community
options.D: Because infectious agents only survive outside the human body

explanation: Great thinking! In community health, we treat the patient while also protecting the wider population from an outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h1)

question: How is 'wellness' best understood in nursing?

options.A: The total elimination of chronic disease through surgical intervention
options.B: The complete absence of any physical or psychological discomfort
options.C: An active, lifelong process of making choices toward optimal well-being
options.D: A temporary state that only occurs when a person is admitted to a ward

explanation: Great job! Wellness isn't just about not being sick; it's a daily, lifelong journey of making healthy choices for your mind and body. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which protozoal infection is mainly spread through contaminated food and water, often causing dysentery?

options.A: Entamoeba histolytica
options.B: Trypanosoma brucei
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Plasmodium falciparum

explanation: Great job! Ingesting Entamoeba histolytica cysts through dirty water or food can lead to painful amebic dysentery. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a patient is lacking fluid (fluid volume deficit)?

options.A: Poor skin turgor
options.B: Dry mucous membranes
options.C: Bounding peripheral pulses
options.D: Concentrated dark urine

explanation: You're doing great! Bounding pulses mean there is plenty of fluid pumping around (or too much!). Dehydration actually causes weak, thready pulses. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why can't a regular surgical mask protect you against true airborne diseases like TB?

options.A: The loose fit lets air and tiny germs slip in through the edges
options.B: The material dissolves in humid hospital rooms
options.C: They only block bacteria, never viruses
options.D: They are only made for patients to wear

explanation: Since surgical masks aren't tightly sealed, air takes the easiest path—right around the sides instead of through the filter! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h2)

question: An older male patient with an enlarged prostate experiences constant urinary dribbling because his bladder is completely full. What is this called?

options.A: Overflow incontinence
options.B: Urge urinary incontinence
options.C: Stress urinary incontinence
options.D: Functional incontinence

explanation: When a blockage stops the bladder from emptying properly, it overfills and leaks small amounts. We call this overflow incontinence. Excellent nursing insight! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why is building trust with community leaders so important for a public health nurse?

options.A: It helps ensure that community members accept and participate in prevention programs
options.B: It eliminates the need to collect health data from individual families
options.C: It guarantees that the nurse will receive financial bonuses from the government
options.D: It allows the nurse to bypass standard medical regulations and protocols

explanation: People listen to leaders they trust. When community leaders back your health programs, the local residents will be much more eager to join in! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h7)

question: How is a public corporation different from a standard government ministry?

options.A: It is completely privately owned by foreign investors
options.B: It only provides care to international travelers
options.C: It has more financial autonomy and generates revenue
options.D: It does not have to follow any government regulations

explanation: Think of public corporations as businesses set up by the government. Unlike normal ministries that only use tax money, they are designed to bring in their own income! [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h1)

question: How is persistent depressive disorder different from major depressive disorder?

options.A: It affects only new mothers following childbirth
options.B: It only occurs during the winter months of the year
options.C: It is a chronic, milder form lasting for two years or longer
options.D: It lasts for exactly two weeks before disappearing entirely

explanation: Spot on! Persistent depressive disorder hangs around for a long time—two years or more—even if the daily symptoms are a bit milder than major depression. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is time considered so critical when dealing with emergency medical conditions?

options.A: Hospital regulations require fast bed turnover
options.B: Insurance companies will not pay for slow care
options.C: Doctors refuse to see patients who wait too long
options.D: Delays can lead to rapid deterioration and death

explanation: In critical emergencies, minutes matter because a failing body system quickly causes permanent harm or death if not supported. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which fasting plasma glucose level is considered diagnostic for diabetes mellitus?

options.A: 100 to 125 mg/dL
options.B: 70 to 99 mg/dL
options.C: Below 60 mg/dL
options.D: 126 mg/dL or higher

explanation: A fasting blood sugar reading of 126 mg/dL or higher measured on two separate occasions is one of the standard diagnostic cutoffs for diabetes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h5)

question: A researcher tests a new diet only on young male athletes in Lagos. Why might this study have low external validity for older women in a rural clinic?

options.A: The laboratory scales were probably out of date
options.B: The researchers forgot to check blood pressures
options.C: The study group does not represent the broader patient population
options.D: The study lacked a budget for food

explanation: You can't easily apply results from young athletes to everyone else! External validity depends on whether your study group actually looks like the wider community. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h3)

question: Which two nutrients are most essential for building and maintaining strong bones?

options.A: Iron and vitamin B12
options.B: Potassium and sodium
options.C: Protein and vitamin C
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: Calcium builds bone structure, and vitamin D is necessary for the body to absorb that calcium properly. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h5)

question: What is the main goal of providing quality reproductive health care?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients visiting clinics
options.B: To increase the cost of hospital operations
options.C: To shorten the working hours of nursing staff
options.D: To reduce maternal and infant mortality rates

explanation: Spot on! High standards in reproductive health directly target the prevention of needless deaths during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of offering family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: To delay physical healing after pregnancy loss
options.B: To check for lower abdominal infections
options.C: To stop pregnancy from ever happening again
options.D: To help prevent rapid, unplanned repeat pregnancies

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps patients protect their bodies and avoid another unplanned pregnancy before they feel ready. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h1)

question: In patient safety, what do we call a 'slip' during a procedure?

options.A: An intentional choice to ignore hospital policy
options.B: A failure to diagnose a patient properly on admission
options.C: An error of execution where the physical action fails
options.D: A complete lack of clinical knowledge about a disease

explanation: A slip happens when you know what to do in your head, but your hands briefly mess up the physical step—like hitting the wrong infusion button by accident. It happens to the best of us! [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h2)

question: Why is medical confidentiality especially critical in occupational health nursing?

options.A: To prevent employers from using private health data to unfairly penalize workers
options.B: To hide mistakes made by the occupational health clinic staff
options.C: To comply with tax laws regarding employee salaries and benefits
options.D: To stop other workers from knowing about common workplace injuries

explanation: Nurses must protect medical information so employees can seek care freely without fear of losing their jobs or facing discrimination. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h2)

question: Which condition often develops later if obsessive-compulsive neurosis is left untreated?

options.A: Antisocial personality disorder
options.B: Schizoaffective disorder
options.C: Major depressive disorder
options.D: Dissociative identity disorder

explanation: You got it! Dealing with constant anxiety and exhaustion day after day often leads to clinical depression down the line. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h7)

question: Drugs like zolpidem and zaleplon belong to which medication family?

options.A: Non-benzodiazepine receptor agonists
options.B: Orexin receptor stimulants
options.C: Barbiturate sedative agents
options.D: Tricyclic antidepressant hypnotics

explanation: Zolpidem and zaleplon are popular non-benzodiazepine hypnotics—often called 'Z-drugs' in the clinic. Great medication to remember for exams! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h3)

question: What happens in the body to cause an erection during sexual arousal?

options.A: Rapid dehydration of the body
options.B: Constriction of the pelvic arteries
options.C: Depletion of adrenal hormones
options.D: Vasocongestion of penile tissues

explanation: Well done! Arousal sends a rush of blood into the spongy tissues of the penis, causing them to fill up (vasocongestion) and create an erection. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h2)

question: Why should nursing students learn about health economics and GNP?

options.A: It equips them to advocate for better resource allocation and health policies
options.B: It removes all administrative duties from the daily nursing routine
options.C: It guarantees an automatic increase in hospital admission capacities
options.D: It allows them to personally invest in pharmaceutical manufacturing companies

explanation: Knowing how money and health connect helps you speak up confidently for better tools, fair pay, and policy changes for your patients. [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h7)

question: How do chemical messengers like cytokines cause those early signs of illness when the incubation period ends?

options.A: They destroy the pathogen's cell wall completely
options.B: They stop the pathogen from entering the bloodstream
options.C: They block nerve signals so the patient feels no pain
options.D: They provoke inflammatory responses that cause visible symptoms

explanation: Great job! These chemical messengers trigger inflammation, which is why you end up with fevers and body aches. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which stage of change describes a person who has not yet considered changing an unhealthy habit?

options.A: Action
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Preparation

question: Why might a breastfeeding mother be given a progestin-only pill instead of a combined pill?

question: Why is performing FGM in a modern hospital still considered unacceptable?

question: Which digital tool is commonly used to send quick appointment reminders straight to a pregnant client's phone?

question: What exactly is a "near miss" in healthcare?

question: How does having a daily work schedule help a client dealing with auditory hallucinations?

question: Where does the lengthwise growth of a long bone happen?

question: What is the main reason for explaining each step of the exam to the patient?

question: What is the term for the network of how food is grown, transported, and sold in a region?

question: Which of the following should you NOT tell a patient who is monitoring their blood pressure at home?

question: What is most important when creating health education posters for a rural Nigerian community?

question: Which of these is an example of a direct medical cost?

question: What is a major *indirect* cost associated with a physical disability?

question: How is tele-nursing different from general telemedicine?

question: Who should be cared for using standard precautions in a hospital?

options.D: Only individuals coughing or showing rashes

question: A patient suddenly struggles to breathe and swells up after getting an antibiotic injection for the first time. What type of drug reaction is this?

options.C: Type B idiosyncratic or allergic reaction
options.D: Type C chronic accumulation reaction

question: What is a defining feature of Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) schemes?

options.B: They are mandatory for all federal government civil servants

question: What is the major black-box warning linked to the long-term use of propylthiouracil (PTU)?

question: What happens during systemic absorption of a topical medication?

question: How does knowing food groups help you during a dietary chat with a patient?

question: What is the ultimate goal of home health nursing?

options.A: Replacing all family involvement in patient care
options.B: Helping the patient achieve maximum independence
options.C: Transferring the patient to a permanent nursing home
options.D: Keeping the patient dependent on daily nursing visits

question: What should you do right after pulling the needle out of a PPD injection site?

options.C: Apply a tight pressure bandage to stop any bleeding
options.D: Clean the skin again with a fresh alcohol swab

question: What does a vulnerability assessment help a healthcare team figure out?

options.A: The personal home addresses of all senior hospital administrative staff
options.B: The exact daily profit margins of local pharmaceutical retail stores
options.C: Which nursing students achieved the highest grades in community health
options.D: Which populations and structures are most at risk during a local hazard

explanation: Spot-on! A vulnerability assessment helps us see who in the community is most likely to suffer, letting us protect them first. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is a main reason why children affected by HIV often drop out of school?

options.C: Mandatory admission into vocational training centers
options.D: Constant medical quarantine inside local hospitals

question: What is the main danger of failing to do regular reassessments in emergency care?

question: Why are Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) so popular for feeding hungry children early in a disaster?

options.B: They taste sweet and only appeal to adults

question: What is the primary goal of Parent Management Training (PMT)?

question: What is an unfavorable budget variance?

question: A nurse is trying to calculate a drug dose, but the screen is cluttered with pop-ups, flashing icons, and tiny text. What is this poor design causing?

question: How does a secondary immune response compare to a primary immune response?

question: What is the main purpose of holding an after-action review (AAR) after responding to a disaster?

options.C: To permanently close down the hospital's emergency department services

question: Why is it so helpful to link diagnostic results directly into the Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

question: How do healthcare workers usually trigger artificial active immunity in patients?

question: A patient visits the clinic with stomach upset, tension headaches, and poor sleep after getting a major promotion at work. What is the most likely cause?

question: How has occupational health nursing changed from the 19th century to the 21st century?

question: Where are interneurons found in the human body?

question: What is the main goal of giving artificial respiration?

question: Why do nurses test for urinary ketones in a pregnant patient with severe vomiting?

question: What makes foetal hemoglobin different from adult hemoglobin?

question: What is the number one goal of requiring a healthcare provider to have a license?

question: What is the main job of muscle spindles?

question: Why are sympathomimetic drugs often called 'fight-or-flight' medications?

question: Which of these nursing actions is a classic example of primary prevention?

question: Why is a silent chest in a patient with severe asthma considered a dangerous emergency?

question: Why do we recommend putting petroleum jelly on a healing biopsy site instead of letting a hard crust form?

question: Where do most absorbed nutrients go immediately after leaving the digestive tract?

question: Why do raw spreadsheets often fail to convince hospital staff to change their practices?

question: Right after an earthquake hits, emergency food, water, and medical teams are rushed to the scene. What phase of disaster management is this?

question: What do we mean by the 'second victim' in healthcare?

question: At what age does the posterior fontanelle usually close up?

question: How does a Just Culture handle an honest human mistake made by a dedicated nurse?

options.D: By publicly shaming the nurse during a staff meeting

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention?

options.A: Running a stress-reduction workshop for healthy adults
options.B: Screening high school students for early signs of depression
options.C: Administering emergency life support for a drug overdose
options.D: Providing long-term rehabilitation for chronic schizophrenia

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and prompt treatment to stop mild symptoms from becoming severe disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h2)

question: How do open drug markets make self-medication so easy?

options.A: They provide easy, unrestricted access to potent drugs without a prescription
options.B: They operate under strict government supervision to prevent drug abuse
options.C: They offer free laboratory tests to help patients choose the right drug
options.D: They employ clinical pharmacologists who safely evaluate every customer

explanation: Open markets let anyone walk in with cash and walk out with strong, serious medications—no questions asked by a medical professional. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does listening to patient and family feedback help nurses improve the ward?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for scientific research articles
options.B: It allows nurses to spend less time documenting patient charts
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will receive increased government funding
options.D: It reveals gaps in care that clinical staff might easily overlook

explanation: Patients experience the hospital from a totally different angle. Their feedback helps us catch little things we might miss while rushing through our busy shifts. [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which type of study focuses on describing the person, place, and time of a disease outbreak?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Analytical study
options.C: Clinical trial
options.D: Descriptive study

explanation: Correct! Descriptive studies simply paint the picture of who is sick, where they are, and when it happened. You're crushing it! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a post-incident debriefing or 'hot wash' session?

options.A: To review performance, identify communication failures, and improve future responses
options.B: To audit employee payroll and overtime hours for budget approval
options.C: To assign personal blame and punishment to staff members who made mistakes
options.D: To celebrate the end of the shift with recreational activities

explanation: Debriefs aren't about pointing fingers; they're safe spaces to figure out what went well and what can be fixed for next time. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h7)

question: Besides personal interest, what else does a researcher need for their chosen topic?

options.A: A personal relationship with the hospital director
options.B: A degree in computer engineering
options.C: Relevant clinical expertise and methodological skills
options.D: At least ten years of experience living abroad

explanation: You need to understand the clinical setting and know how to collect and look at your data properly to get trustworthy results. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h5)

question: How does diluting a medication help when giving tiny doses to an infant?

options.A: It completely eliminates all potential drug side effects
options.B: It makes measuring a larger volume more accurate
options.C: It prevents the infant from developing a drug allergy
options.D: It shortens the half-life of the drug in the body

explanation: Measuring tiny drops like 0.2 mL can be nerve-wracking. Diluting lets you draw up a slightly bigger, much safer-to-measure amount! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h2)

question: If a patient is admitted to a psychiatric ward while still secretly taking traditional herbal mixtures, what is a top nursing worry?

options.A: Potential adverse drug interactions with prescribed psychiatric medications
options.B: The cost of traditional herbs will bankrupt the hospital
options.C: The patient will immediately stop eating hospital food
options.D: The patient will refuse to wear hospital gowns

explanation: Crucial nursing insight! Combining unmeasured herbs with hospital psychiatric drugs can cause dangerous chemical clashes and unexpected side effects. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why do healthcare workers often resist new changes introduced in the hospital?

options.A: Fear of the unknown and disruption to established routines
options.B: A lack of interest in improving patient care quality
options.C: Federal laws prohibiting changes to shift schedules
options.D: Desire to challenge the authority of the nursing director

explanation: Change can feel scary because it disrupts familiar habits. Good leaders understand this and communicate clearly to support their team through it. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h6)

question: A family member stops going to work to care for a sick relative. What type of cost is this?

options.A: Direct medical cost
options.B: Fixed facility cost
options.C: Intangible cost
options.D: Indirect cost

explanation: When a caregiver misses work to help a patient, the lost income is counted as an indirect cost. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h3)

question: A newly admitted patient is too weak to stand on the weighing scale. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Record the weight from their visit five years ago
options.B: Skip the weight measurement until discharge
options.C: Use a bed scale or lift scale for an accurate baseline
options.D: Ask a family member to guess the patient's weight

explanation: Spot on! An accurate baseline weight is key for tracking fluid balance and nutrition, so specialized scales are a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h2)

question: In which part of our digestive system does most nutrient absorption happen?

options.A: Oral cavity
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Large intestine
options.D: Small intestine

explanation: You got it! The small intestine has tiny finger-like folds (villi) that create a huge surface area to soak up all the good nutrients into our bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h5)

question: What is the main goal of doing an economic appraisal in healthcare?

options.A: To compare costs and outcomes of healthcare choices
options.B: To calculate the exact monthly salary of hospital staff
options.C: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the ward
options.D: To diagnose complex medical conditions in a laboratory

explanation: Think of this as checking if a treatment gives you good value. Economic appraisals look at both the money spent and the health benefits gained so hospitals can make smart choices. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is preventing diseases just as important as treating sick patients in the community?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications or hospitals
options.B: It ensures that doctors only work during morning hours
options.C: It stops illnesses before they spread and overwhelms the health system
options.D: It removes the responsibility of health from the individual person

explanation: Prevention saves lives and keeps our clinics from getting completely overwhelmed. Stopping trouble early is always a win! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h4)

question: A nurse in a busy rural clinic runs out of sterile gloves during an emergency wound dressing. What is the safest clinical action?

options.A: Obtain fresh supplies or use available clean alternatives according to protocol, avoiding unsafe shortcuts
options.B: Cancel the procedure and send the patient home without care
options.C: Perform the procedure barehanded to save time
options.D: Reuse a discarded pair of gloves after washing them with cold water

explanation: Shortages should never excuse compromising basic safety; nurses must secure proper supplies or follow approved institutional alternatives. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which waste product from muscle breakdown is checked in lab tests to see how well kidneys are working?

options.A: Creatinine
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: Spot on! Creatinine is a normal waste product from our muscles. If the kidneys aren't filtering well, this level builds up in the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T7#GNS121_U2_T7_h4)

question: In professional nursing, what does 'responsibility' actually mean?

options.A: The personal ability to influence others without holding a title
options.B: The official legal right to command subordinate workers
options.C: The financial reward given for working extra night shifts
options.D: The obligation to perform assigned tasks and achieve expected results

explanation: Think of responsibility as your professional duty—it's the commitment to get your assigned nursing tasks done properly and safely! [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which of these is a biological factor that affects emotional health?

options.A: Monthly income and housing stability
options.B: Access to community parks and recreation
options.C: Cultural beliefs about mental illness
options.D: Genetic predispositions and neurochemistry

explanation: Biological factors are all about what's happening inside our bodies—like our genes, physical health, and brain chemistry. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h2)

question: Who are peer champions in the context of sustaining ward improvements?

options.A: Hospital security officers who check building entry badges
options.B: Senior pharmacists who manage drug storage and inventory
options.C: Respected staff nurses who mentor newcomers and keep protocols alive
options.D: External consultants hired from foreign countries for yearly audits

explanation: Peer champions are vital because they guide junior colleagues and maintain standards long after formal project trainers leave. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main job of a supercomputer in medical research?

options.A: Displaying continuous bedside vital sign waveforms
options.B: Printing hospital administrative billing invoices
options.C: Running daily electronic charting for individual patient rooms
options.D: Performing complex calculations for research like genomic sequencing

explanation: Spot on! Supercomputers are extreme number-crunchers used for massive scientific breakthroughs like decoding human genes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h6)

question: What does an Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) blood test look for?

options.A: The amount of oxygen bound to hemoglobin
options.B: The total number of red blood cells in circulation
options.C: The presence of bacterial pathogens in the bloodstream
options.D: The presence of antibodies that attack the body's own cell nuclei

explanation: An ANA test checks for rogue antibodies that target the control center (nucleus) of our cells, which helps doctors spot systemic autoimmune issues. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which material is most commonly used to make everyday condoms?

options.A: Cotton
options.B: Silicone
options.C: Leather
options.D: Latex

explanation: You got this! Latex is the go-to material for modern condoms because it is strong, stretchy, and reliable at blocking sperm and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: You are deployed to a rural village experiencing a sudden cholera outbreak. What should be your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Instructing residents to swim only in stagnant agricultural ponds
options.B: Administering broad-spectrum topical creams to all affected skin areas
options.C: Collecting industrial factory waste samples from local rivers
options.D: Providing oral rehydration therapy and promoting safe drinking water practices

explanation: Brilliant! Saving lives means stopping dehydration right away with oral rehydration therapy and making sure patients stop drinking contaminated water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h8)

question: Which of these actions is a dangerous violation of medication safety rules?

options.A: Checking the expiry date on a drug vial prior to preparing the injection
options.B: Signing off that you gave a medication before the patient actually swallows it
options.C: Asking a patient to state their full name before handing them oral tablets
options.D: Verifying a calculated pediatric dose with a senior colleague

explanation: Spot on! Never sign for a drug before it's taken. Documenting care before it happens falsifies records and puts patients at risk. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h3)

question: Roughly what percentage of surface contaminants can be removed just by taking off a victim's outer clothes?

options.A: About 80 percent
options.B: Exactly 50 percent
options.C: Only 5 percent
options.D: Nearly 100 percent

explanation: Fascinating fact! Simply stripping off contaminated outer clothing gets rid of the vast majority of harmful chemicals right away. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which statement best describes how research studies treat hypotheses?

options.A: The hypothesis is always proven wrong in clinical trials
options.B: Data either supports the hypothesis or fails to support it
options.C: A successful study proves the hypothesis is an absolute law
options.D: Hypotheses are proven true without needing statistical tests

explanation: Science is a journey! We don't claim absolute truth from one study; our data simply supports our guess or tells us to look closer. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h7)

question: What goes wrong in the body to cause the symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS)?

options.A: Accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques in the temporal lobes
options.B: Excessive release of glutamate causing immediate excitotoxicity
options.C: Thrombus formation blocking blood flow in the middle cerebral artery
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of central nervous system myelin

explanation: In MS, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and strips away the protective myelin coating on nerve fibers, slowing down signals. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h7)

question: What is the main difference between simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion?

options.A: Simple diffusion moves nutrients against a gradient, while facilitated moves with it
options.B: Simple diffusion only moves water, while facilitated diffusion moves solids
options.C: Simple diffusion requires ATP, while facilitated diffusion does not
options.D: Simple diffusion does not use carrier proteins, while facilitated diffusion does

explanation: Think of simple diffusion as slipping easily through a gap, while facilitated diffusion needs special protein 'doorkeepers' to help molecules across the membrane. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h3)

question: How does quality improvement differ from traditional quality assurance?

options.A: Quality improvement ignores patient outcomes to focus entirely on financial savings.
options.B: Quality assurance is only used in surgical units, while quality improvement is used everywhere.
options.C: Quality improvement looks at fixing underlying processes, while quality assurance often focuses on finding faults after they happen.
options.D: Quality assurance focuses on ongoing system redesign, while quality improvement looks for individual faults.

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Old-school quality assurance usually looks backward to find someone to blame, but quality improvement looks forward to fix the process so it works smoothly. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h1)

question: What does variability tell us about a set of patient data?

options.A: The exact middle value of a data set
options.B: The total sum of all recorded patient observations
options.C: The spread or scatter of data points around a central value
options.D: The most frequently occurring measurement in a study

explanation: Great job thinking about data! Variability simply shows how bunched up or spread out patient numbers are from the average. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T5#GNS217_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why do mental health issues in displaced populations often get missed during standard medical checks?

options.A: Trauma only affects physical organs and never the nervous system.
options.B: Healthcare workers are legally forbidden from asking about mood.
options.C: Displaced persons do not experience psychological stress.
options.D: Patients frequently present with physical symptoms masking their emotional distress.

explanation: Emotional pain doesn't always look like crying. Often, patients show up with physical complaints like constant headaches, stomach aches, or fatigue when deep down they are dealing with trauma. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of demographic data found in an EHR?

options.A: Active blood pressure medication list

options.D: Patient home address and phone number

explanation: Demographics refer to basic personal and contact details rather than clinical test results or treatments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: A nurse draws up the wrong drug dose, but catches the mistake before giving it to the patient. What is this called?

options.A: A near miss
options.B: A sentinel event
options.C: A preventable error
options.D: An adverse event

explanation: That's a close one! A 'near miss' is when a mistake almost happens but gets caught just in time before it can hurt anyone. Excellent catch by the nurse! [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h1)

question: Even though we only need micronutrients in tiny amounts, why can lacking them still make someone very sick?

options.A: Micronutrients are the only source of energy for the heart muscle
options.B: Large amounts of carbohydrates destroy all stored vitamins in the liver
options.C: Vitamins and minerals convert directly into body fat during digestion
options.D: Micronutrients regulate essential chemical reactions despite being needed in small amounts

explanation: You got it! Think of vitamins and minerals like car keys or spark plugs—you don't need a huge pile of them, but without them, the engine won't start! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h4)

question: A patient with severe schizophrenia is losing weight because they never cook or buy groceries. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: A physical inability to chew or swallow solid food
options.B: An allergic reaction to standard grocery store items
options.C: Negative symptoms like apathy and lack of drive
options.D: A deliberate choice to fast for religious reasons

explanation: Well done! Negative symptoms such as avolition can rob patients of the motivation needed to plan and execute daily tasks like cooking. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: What is a major systemic challenge frequently facing primary health care centers in Nigeria today?

options.A: Too many operational hospitals with zero patients
options.B: Excessive supplies of clean water and electricity
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of highly paid medical doctors in every village
options.D: Chronic underfunding and shortages of essential drugs

question: If a nursing mother's diet lacks enough nutrients, how does her body manage to produce breast milk?

options.A: The body absorbs extra nutrients directly from the air
options.B: Milk production stops completely until diet improves
options.C: The body draws from maternal stores to maintain milk
options.D: Breast milk loses all its essential nutrients instantly

explanation: Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs! If diet falls short, the mother's body will use its own stored nutrients to keep the milk flowing. Great job understanding maternal priority! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h1)

question: Why are community health nurses usually the first to notice an unusual disease cluster?

options.A: Because they only review paperwork sent from foreign countries
options.B: Because they spend all their time working in national research labs
options.C: Because they focus entirely on hospital financial accounting
options.D: Because they interact daily with families and local groups

explanation: Community nurses are right on the ground! Because you work closely with local families every day, you're in the best position to spot when something feels off. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the go-to medication used to stop and prevent seizures in severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Diazepam tablets

options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Paracetamol syrup

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is our absolute best friend for preventing and stopping eclamptic fits. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why must used needles and medical waste be disposed of with extreme care in a disaster camp?

options.A: To provide building materials for temporary shelters
options.B: To make the garbage bags look neat and tidy
options.C: To keep the air smelling fresh for the residents
options.D: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and biological contamination

explanation: Throwing sharps around carelessly can easily injure children playing nearby or fellow health workers. Safety first, always! [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h7)

question: A patient is taking extra fiber for constipation. What important advice must you give them?

options.A: Increase fluid intake significantly alongside the extra fiber
options.B: Take the fiber supplement immediately before going to bed
options.C: Cook all high-fiber vegetables until they are completely soft
options.D: Eliminate all fats from the diet to make the fiber work faster

explanation: Well done! Fiber acts like a sponge—if patients don't drink enough water with it, it can actually make constipation worse or cause a blockage. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h5)

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body against infectious diseases?

options.A: By lowering body temperature during an active viral infection
options.B: By destroying bacteria directly with heavy doses of antibiotics
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce protective antibodies
options.D: By cleaning harmful toxins directly out of the bloodstream

explanation: Vaccines teach the immune system to recognize and fight off specific germs safely. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why are psychiatric nurses often the first to spot early signs of relapse in parole patients?

options.A: They spend all their time reviewing legal documents in offices.
options.B: They have close, regular contact through home visits and clinic checks.
options.C: They hold the sole legal power to revoke parole on their own.
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers trained in mental health.

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses build close bonds and check in regularly, they are usually the first to notice subtle shifts in a patient's behavior. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h7)

question: A local clinic plans to administer 4,000 curative injections over the next quarter without a waste factor. If each injection needs one syringe, how many syringes should be ordered?

question: A patient stops shaking after a seizure, falls into a deep, snoring sleep, and feels confused when woken up. What nursing term describes this phase?

options.A: Aura phase
options.B: Tonic phase
options.C: Postictal phase
options.D: Clonic phase

explanation: Great job! 'Post' means after, and 'ictal' refers to the seizure. This recovery period is the postictal phase. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h5)

question: Who discovered penicillin, our first natural antibiotic?

options.A: Joseph Lister
options.B: Edward Jenner
options.C: Paul Ehrlich
options.D: Alexander Fleming

explanation: Fleming spotted mold growing on a stray petri dish, and noticed it killed the surrounding bacteria. A lucky accident that changed medicine forever! [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h5)

question: Who is famous for unchaining patients at the Bicêtre Hospital in Paris during the moral treatment era?

options.A: Philippe Pinel
options.B: Dorothea Dix
options.C: Linda Richards
options.D: Sigmund Freud

explanation: Philippe Pinel was a true hero for human rights. He stepped up, took off the chains, and insisted that psychiatric patients deserved respect and dignity. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h3)

question: A newly admitted resident is very quiet and refuses to interact with others. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Immediately discharge the resident back home for family care
options.B: Prescribe a mild sedative medication to calm their anxiety
options.C: Ignore the behavior since adjustment to a new home takes weeks
options.D: Conduct a comprehensive holistic assessment including psychological and social history

explanation: Spot on! Before jumping to conclusions, a warm, thorough assessment helps us find out if they are dealing with depression or fear so we can support them properly. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of defining a 'case' during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: To ensure everyone uses the exact same criteria to count infected people
options.B: To find out which nurse made a charting mistake
options.C: To prove that the hospital is free of bacteria
options.D: To decide which patients must pay for their treatment

explanation: A clear case definition ensures accurate data collection without overcounting or undercounting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the very first step required for MVA instruments immediately after a procedure is finished?

options.A: Placing them into a decontamination solution
options.B: Wrapping them tightly in sterile cloth drapes
options.C: Storing them directly in a warm drying cabinet
options.D: Scrubbing them with dry steel wool pads

explanation: Decontaminating instruments right after use inactivates infectious agents and prevents blood from drying on the plastic surfaces. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: What is the main difference between measurement and evaluation in nursing school?

options.A: Measurement is done by students, while evaluation is done strictly by hospital managers.
options.B: Measurement assigns numbers, while evaluation interprets those numbers to make a judgment.
options.C: Measurement evaluates clinical skills, while evaluation tests written knowledge.
options.D: Measurement focuses on attitudes, while evaluation focuses purely on psychomotor tasks.

explanation: Think of measurement as gathering raw data like your test score (e.g., 75%), while evaluation decides what that score actually means for your progress as a nurse. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: What is the most frequent cause of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)?

options.A: Severe iodine deficiency
options.B: Graves' disease
options.C: Pituitary adenoma
options.D: Hashimoto's thyroiditis

question: A pregnant patient in her 8th week comes in with severe hyperthyroidism. Which medication should the nurse expect the doctor to order?

options.A: Lugol's iodine solution
options.B: Radioactive iodine-131
options.C: Propylthiouracil (PTU)
options.D: Methimazole

explanation: Spot on! PTU is the go-to medication during the first trimester of pregnancy to keep the baby safe from methimazole's risks. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h3)

question: About how much total cerebrospinal fluid does the human body produce every 24 hours?

options.A: 15 milliliters
options.B: 500 milliliters

options.D: 5 liters

question: Why does a severe opioid overdose lead to dangerous breathing problems?

options.A: It causes immediate physical swelling and closure of the main vocal cords
options.B: It depresses the respiratory control center in the brainstem, reducing breathing rate
options.C: It freezes the movement of the diaphragm muscle by destroying motor nerves
options.D: It triggers severe allergic bronchospasm in the small bronchial airways

explanation: Opioids affect the part of the brain that tells the body to breathe, causing breathing to slow down and eventually stop if untreated. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the core idea behind situational leadership in healthcare?

options.A: The best leadership style changes based on the task and staff readiness
options.B: Only senior doctors are qualified to choose leadership styles
options.C: Patient outcomes are completely unrelated to nursing management
options.D: A manager must use the exact same style every day regardless of staff

explanation: Situational leadership is all about flexibility. A great manager matches their approach to the team's experience level and the task at hand. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why should community members be involved in evaluating health projects?

options.A: It stops the government from auditing the facility
options.B: It gives them the legal right to close the clinic down
options.C: It is required only for international funding bodies
options.D: It promotes accountability and shows them the results of their work

explanation: Involving locals in evaluation builds transparency and lets them see how their participation improved community health. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the main difference between major and minor tranquilizers?

options.A: Major tranquilizers treat severe psychosis, whereas minor tranquilizers treat anxiety
options.B: Minor tranquilizers require intravenous administration only
options.C: Major tranquilizers carry zero risk of dependence
options.D: Minor tranquilizers block dopamine pathways exclusively

explanation: They are used for different jobs: major ones handle deep thought disorders, while minor ones tackle everyday anxiety states. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T4#GNS223_U6_T4_h2)

question: A manager wants to check if nurses are consistently signing off on medication times. Which tool is best for this?

options.A: Staff annual performance reviews
options.B: Patient satisfaction surveys
options.C: Hospital financial balance sheets
options.D: Nursing chart audits

question: Which detail is most important to include in the nursing documentation after the procedure?

options.A: The color of the bedsheets on the patient's bed
options.B: The names of all visiting family members present
options.C: The amount and character of gas or stool expelled
options.D: The exact brand name of the lubricant used

question: What is the primary goal of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: To monitor and detect adverse drug reactions to ensure patient safety

options.C: To supervise the physical packaging of pills in pharmacies
options.D: To market new pharmaceutical products to international hospitals
