question: Which of these is a key responsibility of a bedside staff nurse regarding research?

options.A: Questioning outdated routines and asking if there is a better way
options.B: Funding international clinical trials out of personal salary
options.C: Writing complex statistical formulas for textbooks
options.D: Approving the annual budget for hospital research departments

explanation: Spot on! Staying curious and questioning unproven routines is the heartbeat of everyday nursing progress. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h7)

question: A 16-year-old first-time pregnant girl comes to her first antenatal visit. How should the nurse behave to make sure she comes back?

options.A: Offering a friendly, confidential environment free from moral judgment
options.B: Requiring an older family member to answer all questions for her
options.C: Limiting her visit duration to avoid overwhelming her with information
options.D: Scolding her gently for becoming pregnant at such a young age

explanation: Teens often avoid clinics because they fear being scolded or judged. A warm, welcoming, and confidential space builds real trust! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is the main danger of relying only on tradition in nursing care?

options.A: It increases the financial cost of basic hospital linens
options.B: It causes nursing schools to close down unexpectedly
options.C: It makes doctors refuse to work with nursing staff
options.D: It can keep nurses doing things that are outdated or harmful

explanation: When we only follow old routines without questioning them, unsafe or outdated practices can stick around much longer than they should. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of agencies working together in community health?

options.A: It reduces the number of rural health clinics
options.B: It pools resources and expertise to tackle complex health needs
options.C: It puts all healthcare services inside major airports
options.D: It removes the need for nursing licenses

explanation: Exactly! When different agencies team up, they share funding, knowledge, and hands-on help to solve big health problems together. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h8)

question: A nurse throws an empty IV fluid bag with no blood stains into the regular office bin. Is this okay?

options.A: Yes, because it is general non-hazardous waste
options.B: No, intravenous items are always treated as sharps
options.C: No, all plastic items must go into infectious bins
options.D: Yes, provided the bag is shredded first by the nurse

explanation: Great choice! Clean packaging and IV bags that haven't touched blood or body fluids are safe to go into the general waste bin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of development committees in Nigerian primary health care?

options.A: To replace trained doctors in rural clinics
options.B: To encourage community participation and local ownership
options.C: To collect taxes for hospital construction
options.D: To manage federal medical centers directly

explanation: These committees exist to involve local people so they can take charge of their own health needs and partner effectively with health workers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: How would you best describe the peritoneum?

options.A: A thick muscular wall separating the chest and belly
options.B: The outermost layer of the human heart muscle
options.C: The primary filtering unit inside human kidneys
options.D: A serous membrane lining the abdominal cavity

explanation: You've got this! The peritoneum is a smooth, slippery lining that wraps around your tummy wall and internal organs, keeping everything neatly cushioned. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h2)

question: Most plant foods don't have all the essential amino acids, but which of these plant-based foods is a famous exception?

options.A: Rice
options.B: Soy
options.C: Corn
options.D: Wheat

explanation: Soy (found in tofu, soy milk, and tempeh) is wonderful because it is one of the rare plant foods that provides a complete protein source. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h4)

question: Why must a home care plan be flexible rather than completely rigid?

options.A: So the nurse can visit whenever it is convenient for them
options.B: To bypass the need for approval from the primary physician
options.C: To fit smoothly into the patient's personal daily routines
options.D: Because insurance companies change policies every single week

explanation: If a care plan respects and fits into a patient's normal daily habits, they are much more likely to follow it successfully. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h3)

question: What lab results typically point to primary hypothyroidism?

options.A: High TSH and high Free T4
options.B: High TSH and low Free T4
options.C: Low TSH and high Free T4
options.D: Low TSH and low Free T4

explanation: Spot on! When the thyroid slows down, the pituitary panics and pumps out high TSH trying to wake it up, while actual Free T4 levels drop. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h4)

question: A public health team rushes to a village to investigate a sudden outbreak of measles only. What type of assessment are they doing?

options.A: Problem-oriented community diagnosis
options.B: National census data collection
options.C: Hospital morbidity survey
options.D: Comprehensive community diagnosis

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! When we zero in on one specific issue or outbreak instead of looking at the whole community, we call it a problem-oriented approach. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h3)

question: How must Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) be released to properly wake up the pituitary gland?

options.A: Only during deep sleep cycles
options.B: In a continuous steady stream
options.C: In regular pulses
options.D: Once every twenty-four hours

explanation: You nailed it! GnRH loves a rhythmic beat. It has to be released in pulses; if it flows constantly in a steady stream, hormone production actually shuts down. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why is supervised exercise an important part of cardiac rehabilitation after a heart attack?

options.A: It guarantees that plaque will instantly dissolve out of every blocked artery
options.B: It safely strengthens the heart muscle and improves overall cardiovascular endurance
options.C: It stops the nervous system from ever experiencing emotional stress
options.D: it completely eliminates the need to ever take heart medications again

explanation: Gradual, monitored exercise helps the heart adapt and work more efficiently without putting the patient in danger. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why is lactic acid so important during food fermentation?

options.A: It acts as a natural preservative by lowering pH
options.B: It adds a sweet flavor to the food item
options.C: It turns the food liquid before consumption
options.D: It speeds up the rate of food spoilage

explanation: Great job thinking about this! Lactic acid makes the environment too acidic for bad bacteria to survive, which naturally preserves the food. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h2)

question: A patient says they want to stop eating all carbs immediately to lose weight fast. As their nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Ignore their plan and give them a rigid calorie chart
options.B: Encourage them to double their water intake instead
options.C: Help them set smaller, realistic goals for gradual change
options.D: Tell them to stop eating completely for three days

explanation: Brilliant! Slow, steady lifestyle changes stick around much longer than sudden, painful restrictions. Guide them step by step. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h3)

question: What crucial advice should a nurse give a patient taking antibiotics for endometritis?

options.A: Take the pills only when pelvic pain becomes severe
options.B: Double the dose if a single pill is accidentally missed
options.C: Finish the entire prescription even if symptoms improve
options.D: Stop taking the medication as soon as the fever drops

explanation: Always remind patients to finish their drugs! Stopping early lets the strongest surviving bacteria bounce back, causing a relapse or drug resistance. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting quality improvement reviews in a rehab facility?

options.A: To identify safety risks and find ways to improve patient care outcomes
options.B: To increase the cost of hospital admission fees
options.C: To find individual staff members to punish for making mistakes
options.D: To reduce the number of therapy hours required by insurance

explanation: Spot on! Quality improvement is all about making systems safer and patient care better—it's never about assigning blame. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h8)

question: What do we mean by 'donor fatigue' in international health financing?

options.A: Local nurses becoming too exhausted to complete shift handovers
options.B: International partners shifting their focus and funds to newer global crises
options.C: Government officials sleeping through parliamentary budget meetings
options.D: Patients refusing to take donated medications because they are expired

explanation: Donor fatigue happens when foreign funders lose interest or move their money to newer global emergencies, leaving older projects short of cash. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you check when a patient arrives with an acute sting?

options.A: Applying a cold ice pack to reduce swelling
options.B: Assessing airway, breathing, and circulation
options.C: Inquiring about past medical history
options.D: Cleaning the wound with soap and water

explanation: Always ABCs first! Checking airway, breathing, and circulation helps you catch severe allergic reactions or shock before they get out of hand. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake in a paper health register?

options.A: Apply thick correction fluid until the page is blindingly white.
options.B: Scratch it out heavily with a pen until it is totally hidden.
options.C: Draw a single neat line through the mistake, write 'error', and sign beside it.
options.D: Rip out the page and rewrite the whole day's entries.

explanation: Never scribble out or use heavy Tipp-Ex on medical records! A single neat line keeps things legal, honest, and easy to read while showing an official correction was made. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h4)

question: A patient with hypertension is discharged from a federal teaching hospital. What should the local community health nurse do next?

options.A: Wait for the patient to develop a stroke before taking any action
options.B: Tell the patient never to visit the teaching hospital again for any reason
options.C: Monitor blood pressure regularly and check that prescribed drugs are taken correctly
options.D: Throw away the hospital discharge summary and start a new treatment plan

explanation: The nurse ensures continuity of care by supervising medication adherence and monitoring blood pressure at the local level. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)

question: Which facilities typically represent the tertiary level of health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Primary health care dispensaries in rural villages
options.B: Local government maternity and immunization posts
options.C: Private neighborhood patent medicine shops
options.D: Teaching hospitals and specialist medical centers

explanation: Teaching hospitals and specialized federal medical centers provide the highest level of complex tertiary care. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why do we need clear, agreed-upon definitions when collecting data for quality improvement?

options.A: To ensure everyone interprets and measures terms in the exact same way
options.B: To make the research paper long enough for publication
options.C: To increase the financial budget allocated to the nursing unit
options.D: To prove that nurses are working faster than doctors

explanation: Clear definitions mean everyone is speaking the same language, so the data we collect across different shifts is reliable and true. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why do nurses need to review and update diet plans from time to time?

options.A: Because patients get bored eating the same foods for more than three days
options.B: Because hospital regulations require rewriting charts weekly
options.C: Because food items change their vitamin content every single month
options.D: Because client needs, health status, and life circumstances change over time

explanation: Life isn't static, and neither is health! Regular checks ensure the diet plan keeps up with the patient's changing body and life. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h7)

question: Which prevention method helps protect vulnerable people in the community who cannot receive vaccines themselves?

options.A: Shutting down all municipal water treatment plants
options.B: Treating every citizen with broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Building community immunity through high vaccination rates
options.D: Isolating all healthcare workers in private quarters

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, it creates a shield of herd immunity that protects babies, the sick, and others who cannot take vaccines. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)

question: How do modern informatics tools make communication between different healthcare pros much easier?

options.A: By providing a centralized digital hub for notes, labs, and orders
options.B: By allowing patients to directly alter their medication schedules
options.C: By automatically calling doctors whenever a vital sign changes
options.D: By replacing all face-to-face shift change meetings entirely

explanation: Spot on! Having one central digital chart means doctors, nurses, and pharmacists are all looking at the exact same page, reducing miscommunication on the ward. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of a proactive risk mitigation strategy?

options.A: Filing an incident report after a wrong drug was given
options.B: Apologizing to a family after a surgical complication
options.C: Checking emergency crash carts at the start of every shift
options.D: Investigating why a patient fell out of bed last night

explanation: Checking equipment before an emergency happens is proactive because it stops failure before a patient is harmed. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why is having a strong network connection so crucial for electronic health records?

options.A: It allows real-time updating and sharing of patient data across different departments.
options.B: It prevents computer hardware from overheating during heavy computational tasks.
options.C: It converts analog audio alarms into clear digital text messages.
options.D: It automatically increases the storage capacity of the local hard drive.

explanation: Real-time networking means the pharmacy, lab, and your ward see the exact same up-to-the-minute patient info instantly! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major danger when a trapped victim is finally freed from a prolonged crush injury?

options.A: Crush syndrome and acute kidney failure
options.B: Immediate high blood pressure spikes
options.C: Sudden permanent blindness
options.D: Instantaneous bone hardening

question: What is the main purpose of setting up youth-friendly reproductive health clinics in local communities?

options.A: To offer young people a safe, non-judgmental space to access contraception and information
options.B: To track and penalize adolescents who engage in early sexual activity
options.C: To distribute free surgical instruments for home use
options.D: To provide mandatory pregnancy testing for all high school graduates

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics take away the fear of judgment and stigma, making it easy for teenagers to ask questions and get reliable health guidance early on. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)

question: Why is managing chronic symptoms right at home so helpful for a client?

options.A: It allows them to stay comfortable and remain in their familiar surroundings
options.B: It stops the natural aging process from occurring
options.C: It removes the need for any emotional or family support
options.D: It guarantees that they will never need to see a doctor again

explanation: Spot on! There's no place like home. Managing symptoms there keeps clients secure and surrounded by the people and things they love. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h3)

question: An infusion pump won't start until you scan both the patient's ID band and the drug barcode. What kind of safety feature is this?

options.A: A cognitive distraction

question: Which professional helps residents adapt their living spaces to prevent falls and keep moving safely?

options.D: Clinical research pharmacist

question: Why must nurses check for other physical symptoms alongside pain during a palliative assessment?

options.A: Multiple symptoms interact and can make each other worse, like breathlessness causing panic

options.C: Insurance companies only pay for care if three symptoms are treated at once

question: Why are interactive methods like role-play preferred over lecturing for school health instruction?

options.A: They guarantee that students will never fall ill
options.B: They require no preparation from the classroom teacher
options.C: Children prefer reading long medical textbooks
options.D: They actively engage students and improve practical habits

explanation: Interactive learning helps students internalize concepts and apply them to real-life situations better than passive listening. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: When listening to the chest of a patient with lung consolidation, what sound do you usually hear?

question: What is the anatomical term for the neck region?

question: What local Nigerian food group gives us the most energy from complex carbohydrates?

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to improve teamwork communication?

options.D: Applying standardized handover tools during shift changes

explanation: Spot on! Rigid 'don't question senior staff' attitudes are dangerous because they stop junior nurses from speaking up when they spot a safety issue. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the main job of a regular surgical mask?

options.A: To supply extra oxygen

options.C: To block large splashes, sprays, and droplets
options.D: To provide a tight, air-sealed fit around the face

question: What is the main feature of a "geographical community"?

options.A: An online support group for chronic kidney disease
options.B: Physical and natural boundaries like towns or villages
options.C: People who practice the exact same religious faith
options.D: A group of workers sharing the same profession

question: What is the simple difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used only for animals, while quarantine is used exclusively for human beings.

options.C: Isolation is voluntary, while quarantine is always legally enforced by police.
options.D: Isolation separates sick people with a disease, while quarantine separates people exposed to a disease who might become sick.

explanation: Remember: Isolation is for those who are *already sick*, while quarantine is for those who were *exposed* and are waiting to see if they'll fall ill. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h6)

question: Why should nurses look past a patient's physical impairment when providing total patient care?

options.A: To prevent the patient from asking too many questions

options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing mobility aids
options.D: To ensure the hospital bed is kept free for new admissions

explanation: Great thinking! Loneliness and unmet social needs can really slow down a patient's recovery. Holistic nursing means caring for the whole person. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h1)

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of placing a newborn directly on the mother's bare chest (skin-to-skin contact) right after birth?

options.A: It helps stabilize the infant's temperature and blood sugar
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing afterpains
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of newborn jaundice
options.D: It guarantees the infant will latch without any assistance

explanation: Skin-to-skin is magical! The mother's body acts like a natural incubator, helping the baby's breathing, temperature, and blood sugar stay steady. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h8)

question: What makes home health nursing quite different from working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Infection rates are automatically zero in residential homes
options.B: Patients receive no medical equipment at home
options.C: The nurse has less direct control over the physical environment
options.D: Family members are strictly prohibited from providing care

question: Why must diet care in Nigeria make use of local staples like garri, beans, and yams?

options.C: Because imported foreign foods are illegal to prescribe in government hospitals

explanation: Patients find it much easier to stick to meal plans when they use foods they already know, buy, and love eating every day. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing check after a contrast CT scan?

options.A: Evaluating baseline lung sounds for sudden fluid overload

options.D: Encouraging the patient to drink plenty of fluids

question: Which of these is an example of a favorable expense variance for a hospital ward?

options.C: Experiencing a sudden drop in total patient admissions and revenue
options.D: Paying significantly higher overtime wages to staff than planned

explanation: A variance is 'favorable' when you spend less money than you expected while still keeping standards high. Good job staying under budget! [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h5)

question: What is caregiver burnout?

options.A: An allergic reaction to cleaning supplies used in the home
options.B: Physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged caregiving stress
options.C: A sudden medical illness caught from a patient in the hospital
options.D: The legal termination of a home health care contract

explanation: Caregiver burnout happens when family or informal caregivers become overwhelmed by the continuous physical and emotional demands of supporting a relative. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why must you always wash and clean an instrument before disinfecting or sterilizing it?

options.A: To lower the temperature of surgical metal before autoclaving

options.C: To remove visible dirt and organic matter that protect microbes
options.D: To apply liquid chemicals that inhibit microbial growth on living tissue

question: What substance is commonly mixed with pharmaceutical waste during encapsulation to lock it away safely?

options.A: Cement mortar or bitumen
options.B: Dry river sand
options.C: Cooking vegetable oil
options.D: Pure liquid mercury

question: A community health nurse is planning outreach for an area with high youth unemployment. What is the main challenge fresh school leavers usually face?

options.A: A lack of practical work experience and job openings
options.B: Excessive mandatory retirement benefits
options.C: Permanent immunity to common community illnesses
options.D: Severe physical decline due to old age

question: What is the main difference between microvascular and macrovascular diabetic complications?

options.C: The size of the damaged blood vessels
options.D: How fast the symptoms appear after a meal

question: What is the main purpose of preparing a patient for community reintegration before hospital discharge?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital nursing staff
options.B: To test if the patient can survive without any medical supplies
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for health insurance
options.D: To ensure a smooth and safe transition back to home and daily routines

explanation: Community reintegration focuses on equipping the patient and home environment for real-world independence and participation. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h8)

question: What makes a 'prodrug' unique compared to regular medicines?

options.A: It is always given as a liquid injection rather than a pill
options.B: It bypasses the liver completely without ever changing form
options.C: It is given in an inactive form and needs metabolism to become active
options.D: It leaves the body immediately through sweat instead of urine

explanation: A prodrug is like an undercover agent—it starts off inactive when you swallow it, and only wakes up (becomes active) after the body's metabolism works on it. Pretty cool, right? [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the main public health step used to stop leprosy from spreading in a town or village?

options.A: Finding cases early and starting treatment right away
options.B: Washing living areas with heavy chemicals
options.C: Locking all infected people away in isolated camps
options.D: Giving mandatory vaccines to every newborn baby

explanation: Catching cases early and starting medications quickly stops the spread because treatment makes patients non-infectious! Public health in action! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is the main idea behind Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy?

options.A: Using hypnosis to erase painful childhood memories from the mind
options.B: Prescribing high-dose sedatives to keep the patient calm and asleep
options.C: Encouraging the patient to indulge fully in rituals until they get tired
options.D: Exposing the patient to feared triggers while blocking compulsive rituals

explanation: Well done! ERP retrains the brain by facing what triggers the anxiety head-on, while gently holding off on the safety ritual. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h5)

question: A virus is hiding safely inside body cells. Which part of the immune system handles this best?

options.A: The complement protein cascade in the blood plasma
options.B: Innate physical barriers of the skin and mucous membranes
options.C: Humoral immunity via circulating antibodies
options.D: Cell-mediated immunity via cytotoxic T-cells

explanation: Correct! When germs hide inside cells, cytotoxic T-cells are the hit squad that hunts down and destroys those infected cells. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is psychological rehab just as vital as physical detox when treating substance dependence?

options.A: It replaces the need for any nursing observation or vital sign monitoring
options.B: It ensures the patient never experiences physical withdrawal symptoms again
options.C: It addresses underlying triggers and teaches healthy coping skills to prevent relapse
options.D: It is the only way to restore normal kidney and liver function after drug use

explanation: Brilliant! Detox cleans out the body, but rehab tackles the emotional and behavioral roots of addiction so the patient can learn new ways to cope without drugs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main catch when using regular rubbing alcohol to decontaminate equipment?

options.A: It corrodes stainless steel and ruins delicate hinges
options.B: It leaves a sticky residue that attracts dirt and dust
options.C: It evaporates quickly and does not kill bacterial spores
options.D: It is completely ineffective against common viruses

explanation: Alcohol dries up fast (making it hard to keep things wet long enough) and leaves tough bacterial spores completely unfazed. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which symptom is most common in nurses who spend long hours staring at computer screens for charting?

options.A: Numbness in the big toes
options.B: Swelling of the lower legs
options.C: Weakness in the handgrip
options.D: Dry and fatigued eyes

explanation: You got it! When we stare at screens, we tend to blink less, which leaves our eyes feeling dry and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: What tool do Nigerian nurses commonly use in local clinics to track a child's growth and immunization records?

options.A: Cardiovascular risk profile
options.B: Intensive care flow sheet
options.C: Surgical safety checklist
options.D: National Child Health Card

explanation: Correct! The Child Health Card has the WHO growth curves printed right on it, making it easy to track baby's weight during immunization visits. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h8)

question: Which personal protective equipment is essential when caring for a patient with airborne tuberculosis?

options.A: An N95 respirator mask
options.B: A heavy plastic body apron
options.C: Sterile rubber cleaning boots
options.D: A standard cloth face mask

explanation: Tuberculosis travels on tiny airborne nuclei that require tight-fitting respirator filters to prevent inhalation by health workers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h4)

question: What do we call an evaluation check that looks at whether a community can keep up health benefits after funding ends?

options.A: Effectiveness
options.B: Sustainability
options.C: Efficiency
options.D: Relevance

explanation: Sustainability means the project can stand on its own two feet even after outside donors or support leave. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of a physiatrist in a rehabilitation setting?

options.A: Restoring overall function and managing physical medicine
options.B: Managing hospital finances and administrative admissions
options.C: Conducting psychological counseling for depressed patients
options.D: Performing emergency orthopedic surgeries in the operating room

explanation: A physiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in helping patients regain lost physical abilities and managing non-surgical recovery. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which statistical test should you use to compare test scores across three different nursing shifts?

options.A: ANOVA
options.B: Blood pressure monitor
options.C: Chi-Square test
options.D: Independent t-test

explanation: Well done! ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) is your go-to test when you need to compare averages across three or more separate groups. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T15#GNS217_U4_T15_h5)

question: What is a major economic barrier to healthcare access for many low-income families in Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive abundance of free community health centers
options.B: Strict government bans on traditional herbal medicines
options.C: Out-of-pocket payment for medical services and medications
options.D: Mandatory international health insurance for all citizens

explanation: Without broad health insurance, many families have to pay cash directly for consultations, labs, and drugs, which can be tough. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h4)

question: A patient asks why they didn't get antibiotics for a common viral cold. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Viruses live without oxygen, making antibiotics useless.
options.B: Antibiotics destroy healthy human host cells instead.
options.C: Viruses are too large for antibiotics to catch.
options.D: Antibiotics only target bacteria, not viruses.

explanation: It's common for patients to confuse this! Antibiotics only work against bacteria, so they won't help clear up a viral infection. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which group of medications is well-known for causing sexual side effects like low libido or delayed orgasm?

options.A: Topical antifungal creams
options.B: Over-the-counter antacids
options.C: Short-acting inhaled bronchodilators
options.D: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors

explanation: SSRIs are common antidepressants that unfortunately often interfere with sexual desire and climax. Always keep an eye out for this when counseling patients! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T27#GNS312_U1_T27_h3)
